claims.claim: **Most cyanotic episodes in children with CHD are self-limiting.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Let the parent comfort the child**; clinicians use a **minimal handling** approach with a targeted examination.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Prolonged episodes may be life-threatening** and need active treatment with **oxygen and opiates**; involve senior staff and specialists early.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A cyanotic ('tet') spell** is acute cyanosis, or cyanosis worse than the child's baseline — most often in **Tetralogy of Fallot and pulmonary atresia**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mechanism:** a pulmonary–systemic vascular resistance imbalance reduces pulmonary flow and increases right-to-left shunting.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Peak age 2–6 months**; usually triggered by stress — infection, being upset, or on waking.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **History:** known structural heart disease, **hyperpnoea, cyanosis that is severe (worse than usual)**, precipitants (distress, prolonged crying, dehydration, intercurrent illness), lethargy or altered conscious state; older children may have a history of **squatting**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine gently and briefly** so as not to distress the child: compare cyanosis with baseline on **oxygen saturation monitoring**, check perfusion and hydration, and listen for a murmur if possible.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Calm the child — distress can worsen or prolong the spell.** Keep handling minimal and the child with the parent as much as possible.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Place the child in the knee-to-chest position** (lying supine or held upright) to increase systemic vascular resistance.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Investigate after the spell has resolved**, guided by likely precipitants; an **ECG helps exclude an arrhythmia**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Monitor until the spells have resolved and the child is not sedated from opiates.** Discuss ongoing observation and management with Cardiology.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the local paediatric team** for any spell needing treatment; **consider transfer** if ICU admission or Cardiology review is needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge may be considered once** Cardiology has been consulted and the child is unsedated and at baseline.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23
